Summer classes move quick, so you can’t wait until test week to find out what you remember. Stop relying on passive review and start using active recall. Pull the information from memory without your notes. Don’t just look over the material. Practice explaining it. And one of the easiest ways to do this is flashcards. But don’t just flip and recognize answers. Use them like cue cards. Ask why, what, and how. Make yourself answer before flipping, even if you’re struggling. Separate what you get right and wrong, and keep repeating the ones you miss. Then space it out: review one day later, then three days, then seven. In a summer class, consistency matters even more. A little active recall each day can help you keep up, remember more, and feel more confident when it’s time for the exam. #StudyTips #summercourses #activerecall  #flashcards

My childhood dog lived in a pen outside. He had food and water and a flea collar. I'm sure he went to the vet if he was sick but there was not the option for chemotherapy, advanced imaging or extensive dental work. But our dog was loved and cared for. We're in this weird age that everyone wants to do everything for their pet but are shocked at the costs. Advanced veterinary care is very expensive. But it's not required. We need to have realistic expectations for what we can afford for our pet and not blame veterinarians if it's too expensive. #veterinarian #vettech #vetmed

Veterinary professionals have one of the highest suicide rates of any profession. At the same time, many others are leaving veterinary medicine altogether. There isn’t one single reason why, but one thing I wish more people understood is the emotional toll of being told you’re “only in it for the money” or accused of trying to manipulate people simply because you ask for payment for medical care. Veterinary clinics are businesses with staff to pay, equipment to maintain, medications to stock, and hospitals to keep open. None of that changes when a patient is critically ill. Every veterinarian I know wishes every pet could receive every treatment they need regardless of cost, but wanting that and actually being able to provide it for free are two very different things. Before assuming the worst, remember that the person on the other side of the exam table has likely dedicated years of their life, accumulated significant educational debt, and carries the weight of difficult decisions every single day. A little empathy goes a long way, for everyone involved. #VeterinaryMedicine #VetMed #Veterinarian #MentalHealth #TheHonestVet
